chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He was asked, 'What is the matter with the deceased that he discharges semen?' He said: 'The seed from which he was created, it is thrown out.'
ai.seo_question: Why does the deceased discharge semen after death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the nocturnal emission observed in the deceased is the residual seminal fluid (nutfah) from which the body was originally created, expelled during decomposition. This narration, found in al-Kafi, highlights the physical continuity between the origin of human creation and the natural processes of the body after death, offering a tangible sign of the soul's departure. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that bodily signs, even post-mortem, reflect the intrinsic nature of the human constitution as described in Islamic cosmology.
